[1832., “I have suffered, like other writers, from indolence, irresolution, distaste to my work, absence of “inspiration,” and all that : but I have also found that sitting down, however reluctantly, with the pen in my hand, I have never worked for one quarter of an hour without finding myself in full train : so that all the quarter hours, arguings, doubtings and hesitation as to whether I should work or not which I gave way to in my inexperience, I now regard as so much waste, not only of time but, far worse, of energy.” Every word of the card is there, comma inside the closing quotation mark as printed, distaste to (not for) correct. Fourth Period, To the Age of Thirty-Seven, section I is right. FIRST PROBLEM: the card ends at in full train with a full stop where Martineau has a colon and thirty-odd more words. The verifier knew and accepted the cut, citing February, but February’s accepted cuts (Proust, Sewell) each say so in the shipped note; this one ships with an empty note, so the card presents a clause as a finished sentence without telling anyone. Rule 12: nothing minted, and where the text is trimmed, say so plainly. SECOND PROBLEM: p. 144 with 1877 is ambiguous. There are two 1877 first editions, both with Chapman’s Memorials. In the London one (Smith, Elder, 3 vols; autobiographywit01martuoft) the same sentence runs from the foot of p. 189 onto p. 190 of vol. 1. Page 144 is true only of the Boston Osgood two-volume edition, so the source needs Boston or Osgood in it; the corrected line is 123 characters, no dash. Otherwise clean: shipped.js says not shipped, nothing near, Martineau 0 of 3, not banned; in scope (1877), publishable, exactly on the month’s theme; Essay is a fair tag for a prose autobiography in a vocabulary with no Memoir. Fame is the weak leg (not an opening or closing line; it rests on anthology use), which the verifier rightly left to the editor.
